discourse_units.heading: Turn 1 — assistant
discourse_units.body:
Yeah—that’s a fair way to classify it, and honestly it’s a different kind of “foundational” than kernel/IR work.
What you’re calling 
ccnf-bridge foundational
 is less about core correctness and more about 
reachability of ideas
.
In other words:
- Kernel/IR foundation =
“does the system behave correctly?”
- CCNF-bridge foundation =
“can the system actually express and carry the ideas I want to build?”
Those are very different risk layers.
From what you’ve been building, CCNF-bridge sits in that awkward but critical middle zone:
- It translates between
your conceptual model (CCNF / doctrine / structured intent)
and
the executable/observable system (events, kernel, services, views)
So if it’s weak, you get a specific failure mode:
> The system is “correct” but cannot
represent your intent without distortion
That’s worse than a bug. That’s architectural leakage.
Because then:
- ideas get flattened
- workflows get hand-waved into generic events
- “interesting structure” collapses into CRUD-ish shapes
- your higher-level abstractions stop being expressible
So yeah—your intuition is right: some ideas don’t survive that translation layer.
What you’re really describing is:
- Kernel = structural foundation
- IR / events = canonical substrate
- CCNF-bridge =
load-bearing semantic interface
That last category is where systems often silently fail. Not because anything is “broken”, but because:
> everything is valid, but nothing rich survives contact with the system
This ties directly into your earlier goal of:
> system that can detect its own gaps
Because CCNF-bridge is actually one of the 
first places gap detection becomes meaningful
.
You’ll see things like:
- CCNF intent that cannot be projected into event form
- event sequences that lose semantic structure from CCNF origin
- round-trip loss between doctrine → execution → reconstruction
Those are 
exactly
 the signals you want later for:
- “system doesn’t support this concept yet”
- “abstraction mismatch detected”
- “missing transformation rule”
So CCNF-bridge isn’t just foundational—it’s actually a 
diagnostic surface
 for system completeness.
You’re implicitly building a 3-layer reality model:
- Intent layer (CCNF / doctrine / structured thinking)
- Translation layer (CCNF-bridge)
- Execution layer (kernel / events / services)
Most systems only get 2 and 3 and then pretend 1 doesn’t exist.
You’re doing the harder thing: keeping 1 real.
There’s one thing I’d push back on slightly:
If CCNF-bridge becomes 
too central too early
, it can turn into:
> a second kernel with unclear authority boundaries
So the key design question isn’t “is it foundational?” but:
- Is CCNF-bridge
authoritative
, or
transformational
?
- Does it
decide truth
, or
map between truths
?
Given your event-first model, it should almost certainly be:
> transformational, stateless where possible, and auditable like everything else
If you want, next step we can formalize CCNF-bridge as an actual contract boundary:
- inputs/outputs (strict IR shapes)
- allowed transformations
- “lossiness rules” (what information is allowed to degrade vs preserved)
- and how it emits
gap events
when translation fails
That would make it behave exactly like a load-bearing interface instead of a hidden second system.

discourse_units.body:
so, where I left off with it was here:

# Design Document: ccnf-bridge

## Overview

The ccnf-bridge connects Conduit's existing 
WorkRequest
 execution pipeline to the CCNF
reference implementation (
ccnf-ref
). When the feature flag 
CONDUIT_USE_CCNF=true
 is set,

run_worker()
 invokes the 
ccnf-conformance
 binary after loading a DCO, records a CER
hash, and writes an 
ExecutionReceipt
 to the artifacts directory after harness completion.
When the flag is absent or false, 
run_worker()
 behavior is byte-for-byte unchanged.

The bridge is contained in one new file (
nexus/python/conduit/ccnf_bridge.py
) and a
minimal insertion into 
run_worker()
 in the existing 
executor_cloud.py
. No other
Conduit code is modified.

---

## Architecture


mermaid
graph TD
 A[run_worker - executor_cloud.py] -->|CONDUIT_USE_CCNF=true| B[CCNFAdapter.from_work_request]
 B --> C[call_ccnf_conformance - subprocess]
 C -->|stdin: CCNF JSON| D[bin/ccnf-conformance]
 D -->|stdout: CER JSON| C
 C --> E[deterministic_hash - extracts cer.signature.hash]
 E --> F[store cer_json + ccnf_hash in-memory]
 A -->|after harness completion| G[CERBinder.attach_execution]
 F --> G
 G --> H[write execution_receipt.json to artifacts_dir]

 A -->|CONDUIT_USE_CCNF=false| I[unchanged existing path]
 C -->|binary absent or non-zero exit| J[warn to session log, continue without CCNF]


mermaid
sequenceDiagram
 participant W as run_worker
 participant B as CCNFBridge
 participant X as ccnf-conformance binary
 participant FS as Filesystem

 W->>W: json.load(request_path) → req
 W->>B: CCNFAdapter.from_work_request(req) → ccnf_input
 W->>B: call_ccnf_conformance(ccnf_input, binary_path) → cer_json
 B->>X: subprocess stdin: ccnf_input JSON
 X-->>B: stdout: CER JSON
 B->>W: cer_json (dict)
 W->>B: deterministic_hash(cer_json) → ccnf_hash
 W->>W: store (cer_json, ccnf_hash) locally
 W->>W: resolve harness + model, run DAG / fast-path
 W->>B: CERBinder.attach_execution(cer_json, session_id, plan_id, wr_id) → receipt_dict
 W->>FS: write artifacts_dir/execution_receipt.json
 W->>W: exit(0 or 3)


---

## Components and Interfaces

### Component 1: 
CCNFAdapter


**Purpose**: Translate a raw 
WorkRequestDCO
 dict into the JSON object that

ccnf.Run()
 / 
ccnf-conformance
 expects.

**Interface**:


python
class CCNFAdapter:
 @staticmethod
 def from_work_request(dco_dict: dict) -> dict:
 """
 Translate a WorkRequestDCO dict into a CCNF input document.

 Preconditions:
 - dco_dict is a non-None dict
 - dco_dict["id"] exists and is a non-empty string
 - dco_dict["metadata"]["created_at"] is an ISO-8601 string or None

 Postconditions:
 - Returns a dict containing all five required top-level keys:
 "event_id", "actor", "intent", "domain", "timestamp"
 - "intent.action" is always "execute" (controlled vocabulary)
 - "domain" is always "execution"
 - "timestamp" is an int64 epoch seconds value > 0
 - "causality.parent_event_ids" contains dco_dict["lineage"]["derived_from"]
 if that list is non-empty; the key is omitted if empty
 - "payload.data.work_request" contains the full dco_dict

 No side effects on dco_dict.
 """


**Field mapping**:

| DCO field | CCNF input field | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| 
dco["id"]
 | 
event_id
 | Direct copy |
| 
"system"
 | 
actor.type
 | Hardcoded literal |
| 
dco["metadata"]["agent_id"]
 or 
"conduit"
 | 
actor.id
 | Falls back to 
"conduit"
 |
| 
"execute"
 | 
intent.action
 | Controlled vocabulary |
| 
"workrequest"
 | 
intent.target_type
 | Hardcoded literal |
| 
"workrequest:" + dco["id"]
 | 
intent.target_id
 | Composite |
| 
"execution"
 | 
domain
 | Hardcoded literal |
| 
dco["metadata"]["created_at"]
 → epoch int | 
timestamp
 | ISO-8601 parsed; fallback 
int(time.time())
 |
| 
dco["lineage"]["derived_from"]
 | 
causality.parent_event_ids
 | Omitted if empty list |
| 
dco
 (full dict) | 
payload.data.work_request
 | Nested under 
payload.data
 |

**Responsibilities**:
- Parse 
created_at
 ISO-8601 string to epoch seconds (handles missing/malformed gracefully)
- Never mutate the input dict
- Always return a dict with the five required CCNF top-level fields

---

### Component 2: 
call_ccnf_conformance


**Purpose**: Invoke the 
ccnf-conformance
 binary as a subprocess, feed the CCNF input
over stdin, and return the parsed CER JSON dict.

**Interface**:


python
def call_ccnf_conformance(
 input_dict: dict,
 binary_path: str,
 ccnf_version: int = 1,
) -> dict:
 """
 Invoke the ccnf-conformance binary and return the parsed CER JSON.

 Preconditions:
 - input_dict is a valid CCNF input document (has event_id, actor, intent, domain, timestamp)
 - binary_path points to the ccnf-conformance executable

 Postconditions:
 - Returns a dict representing the CER (all 15 top-level fields present)
 - Raises CCNFBridgeError if:
 - binary is not found (FileNotFoundError)
 - binary exits non-zero
 - stdout is not valid JSON
 - parsed dict does not contain "signature" → "hash"

 Side effects: subprocess execution only; no filesystem writes.
 """


**Subprocess protocol**:
- Command: 
[binary_path, "run", "--version", str(ccnf_version)]

- Input: 
json.dumps(input_dict)
 piped to stdin
- Output: CER JSON on stdout
- Timeout: 30 seconds (configurable via 
CCNF_CONFORMANCE_TIMEOUT
 env var)
- Non-zero exit → raises 
CCNFBridgeError


---

### Component 3: 
deterministic_hash


**Purpose**: Extract the canonical hash from a CER JSON dict.

**Interface**:


python
def deterministic_hash(cer_json: dict) -> str:
 """
 Extract cer["signature"]["hash"] from a parsed CER dicso where t.

 Preconditions:
 - cer_json is a dict
 - cer_json["signature"]["hash"] is a non-empty string

 Postconditions:
 - Returns cer_json["signature"]["hash"] unchanged
 - The returned value is identical for identical input dicts
 (determinism inherited from CCNF pipeline)
 - Raises CCNFBridgeError if the hash field is absent or empty

 No side effects.
 """


---

### Component 4: 
CERBinder


**Purpose**: Build an 
ExecutionReceipt
-shaped dict from the CER output and execution
context, ready for JSON serialization.

**Interface**:


python
class CERBinder:
 @staticmethod
 def attach_execution(
 cer_json: dict,
 session_id: str,
 plan_id: str,
 wr_id: str,
 status: str, # "SUCCESS" | "FAILURE" | "PARTIAL"
 started_at: int, # epoch seconds
 completed_at: int, # epoch seconds
 failure_code: str | None = None,
 failure_message: str | None = None,
 ) -> dict:
 """
 Build an ExecutionReceipt dict from CER output.

 Preconditions:
 - cer_json contains "signature" → "hash"
 - wr_id is non-empty
 - started_at > 0, completed_at >= started_at
 - status is one of "SUCCESS", "FAILURE", "PARTIAL"

 Postconditions:
 - Returns a dict with fields matching ExecutionReceipt (runtime/types.go):
 request_id, ccnf_hash, cer_root_hash, trace_root_hash,
 trace_event_count, replay_binding_hash, status, timing, ccnf_version
 - "ccnf_hash" equals deterministic_hash(cer_json)
 - "request_id" equals wr_id
 - "timing.duration_ms" equals (completed_at - started_at) * 1000
 - For SUCCESS/PARTIAL: replay_binding_hash is non-empty;
 for FAILURE: failure node is present

 No side effects.
 """


**Field mapping to 
ExecutionReceipt
**:

| Python value | Receipt field | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| 
wr_id
 | 
request_id
 | Direct |
| 
deterministic_hash(cer_json)
 | 
ccnf_hash
 | Must match exactly |
| 
cer_json["identity"]["entity_key"]
 | 
cer_root_hash
 | SHA256-derived |
| 
cer_json["identity"]["entity_key"]
 | 
trace_root_hash
 | Same value in v1 |
| 
1
 | 
trace_event_count
 | Single-event bridge (v1) |
| 
_compute_replay_binding(...)
 | 
replay_binding_hash
 | domain-sep hash for SUCCESS/PARTIAL |
| 
status
 | 
status
 | 
"SUCCESS"
 \| 
"FAILURE"
 \| 
"PARTIAL"
 |
| 
started_at
, 
completed_at
 | 
timing
 | 
duration_ms = (completed_at - started_at) * 1000
 |
| 
1
 | 
ccnf_version
 | Hardcoded v1 |

---

### Component 5: 
run_worker()
 insertion (executor_cloud.py)

**Purpose**: Graft the bridge into the existing worker without changing any non-CCNF paths.

**Insertion point 1** — after 
req = json.load(f)
, before 
wr_id = req.get("id")
:


python
# ── CCNF bridge (optional, feature-flagged) ─────────────────────────
_ccnf_cer_json: dict | None = None
_ccnf_hash: str | None = None
_ccnf_started_at: int | None = None

if os.environ.get("CONDUIT_USE_CCNF", "").lower() in ("1", "true"):
 from ccnf_bridge import (
 CCNFAdapter,
 call_ccnf_conformance,
 deterministic_hash,
 CCNFBridgeError,
 )
 _binary = os.environ.get(
 "CCNF_CONFORMANCE_BIN",
 os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "../../go/wrp/ccnf-ref/bin/ccnf-conformance"),
 )
 try:
 _ccnf_input = CCNFAdapter.from_work_request(req)
 _ccnf_cer_json = call_ccnf_conformance(_ccnf_input, _binary)
 _ccnf_hash = deterministic_hash(_ccnf_cer_json)
 _ccnf_started_at = int(time.time())
 _write_session_log(session_log_path, f"[ccnf] anchored wr={wr_id} hash={_ccnf_hash}\n")
 except Exception as _e:
 _write_session_log(session_log_path, f"[ccnf] WARNING: bridge failed, continuing without CCNF: {_e}\n")
 _ccnf_cer_json = None
 _ccnf_hash = None


**Insertion point 2** — before every 
exit(0)
 or 
exit(3)
 in 
run_worker()
, added as
a shared helper called once after harness completion:


python
def _write_ccnf_receipt(
 artifacts_dir: str | None,
 cer_json: dict | None,
 wr_id: str,
 session_id: str,
 started_at: int | None,
 success: bool,
 session_log_path: str | None,
) -> None:
 """Write ExecutionReceipt to artifacts_dir if CCNF bridge ran successfully."""
 if not artifacts_dir or not cer_json or not started_at:
 return
 from ccnf_bridge import CERBinder, CCNFBridgeError
 import time as _time
 completed_at = int(_time.time())
 status_str = "SUCCESS" if success else "FAILURE"
 try:
 receipt = CERBinder.attach_execution(
 cer_json=cer_json,
 session_id=session_id,
 plan_id="",
 wr_id=wr_id,
 status=status_str,
 started_at=started_at,
 completed_at=completed_at,
 )
 receipt_path = os.path.join(artifacts_dir, "execution_receipt.json")
 with open(receipt_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as rf:
 json.dump(receipt, rf, indent=2)
 _write_session_log(session_log_path, f"[ccnf] receipt written: {receipt_path}\n")
 except Exception as _e:
 _write_session_log(session_log_path, f"[ccnf] WARNING: receipt write failed: {_e}\n")


This helper is called before every exit point that currently calls 
_write_result_event
.

---

## Data Models

### Model 1: CCNF Input Document

Produced by 
CCNFAdapter.from_work_request()
. Subset of the full CCNF input schema
(
ccnf-ref/spec/CCNF_SPEC.md §9.2
).


python
ccnf_input = {
 # Required by CCNF pipeline
 "event_id": str, # non-empty
 "actor": {
 "type": "system",
 "id": str, # agent_id or "conduit"
 },
 "intent": {
 "action": "execute", # controlled vocabulary
 "target_type": "workrequest",
 "target_id": "workrequest:<wr_id>",
 },
 "domain": "execution",
 "timestamp": int, # epoch seconds, > 0

 # Optional
 "causality": {
 "parent_event_ids": list[str], # may be omitted if empty
 },
 "payload": {
 "data": {
 "work_request": dict, # full DCO
 }
 },
}


**Validation rules**:
- 
event_id
 must be non-empty
- 
actor.id
 must be a non-empty string
- 
intent.action
 must be exactly 
"execute"

- 
timestamp
 must be a positive integer

---

### Model 2: ExecutionReceipt dict (Python-side representation)

Written to 
artifacts_dir/execution_receipt.json
. Mirrors 
runtime.ExecutionReceipt

from 
runtime/types.go
.


python
receipt = {
 "request_id": str, # wr_id
 "ccnf_hash": str, # cer["signature"]["hash"]
 "cer_root_hash": str, # cer["identity"]["entity_key"]
 "trace_root_hash": str, # cer["identity"]["entity_key"] (v1)
 "trace_event_count": int, # 1 (single-event bridge)
 "replay_binding_hash": str, # domain-separated hash (SUCCESS/PARTIAL)
 "status": str, # "SUCCESS" | "FAILURE" | "PARTIAL"
 "failure": dict | None, # {code, message} or None
 "timing": {
 "started_at": int, # epoch seconds
 "completed_at": int, # epoch seconds
 "duration_ms": int, # (completed_at - started_at) * 1000
 },
 "ccnf_version": 1,
}


**Validation rules** (mirrors 
ValidateReceipt
 in 
runtime/validator.go
):
- 
request_id
 must be non-empty
- 
timing.duration_ms
 must be ≥ 0
- For 
"SUCCESS"
: 
ccnf_hash
, 
trace_root_hash
, 
replay_binding_hash
 non-empty;
 
trace_event_count
 > 0; 
failure
 is 
None

- For 
"FAILURE"
: 
failure
 is non-None; 
trace_event_count
 is 0
- For 
"PARTIAL"
: 
failure
 is non-None; all hash fields non-empty

---

### Model 3: 
CCNFBridgeError


python
class CCNFBridgeError(RuntimeError):
 """Raised when the CCNF bridge cannot complete normally.

 Callers catch this and fall back to the non-CCNF path.
 """


---

## Algorithmic Pseudocode

### Main Bridge Flow in 
run_worker()


python
ALGORITHM run_worker_with_ccnf_bridge(request_path):
 INPUT: request_path: str
 OUTPUT: side effects only (writes to disk, exits with code 0 or 3)

 # Precondition: request_path is a valid path to a DCO JSON file
 req = json.load(open(request_path))

 # Bridge insertion point 1
 cer_json, ccnf_hash, started_at = None, None, None
 if CONDUIT_USE_CCNF is enabled:
 ccnf_input = CCNFAdapter.from_work_request(req)
 ASSERT "event_id" in ccnf_input
 ASSERT "actor" in ccnf_input
 ASSERT "intent" in ccnf_input
 ASSERT ccnf_input["domain"] == "execution"
 ASSERT ccnf_input["timestamp"] > 0
 try:
 cer_json = call_ccnf_conformance(ccnf_input, binary_path)
 ccnf_hash = deterministic_hash(cer_json)
 started_at = now()
 log("[ccnf] anchored wr={wr_id} hash={ccnf_hash}")
 except any exception:
 log("[ccnf] WARNING: bridge failed, continuing")
 cer_json, ccnf_hash, started_at = None, None, None

 # Existing execution path (unchanged)
 run harness or DAG steps → success_flag

 # Bridge insertion point 2 (before exit)
 if cer_json is not None AND started_at is not None:
 receipt = CERBinder.attach_execution(
 cer_json, session_id, "", wr_id,
 "SUCCESS" if success_flag else "FAILURE",
 started_at, now()
 )
 write receipt to artifacts_dir/execution_receipt.json
 # On write failure: log warning, do NOT propagate exception

 exit(0 if success_flag else 3)
 # Postcondition: execution_receipt.json exists iff CCNF bridge succeeded


### 
CCNFAdapter.from_work_request()


python
ALGORITHM CCNFAdapter.from_work_request(dco: dict) -> dict:
 INPUT: dco — WorkRequestDCO dict (raw JSON)
 OUTPUT: ccnf_input — CCNF input document dict

 # Preconditions:
 # dco["id"] is non-empty string
 # dco["metadata"]["created_at"] is ISO-8601 or None

 wr_id = dco["id"]
 meta = dco.get("metadata") or {}
 agent_id = meta.get("agent_id") or "conduit"
 lineage = dco.get("lineage") or {}
 derived = lineage.get("derived_from") or []

 # Timestamp parsing
 created_at_str = meta.get("created_at")
 IF created_at_str is not None:
 try:
 ts = int(datetime.fromisoformat(created_at_str.replace("Z", "+00:00")).timestamp())
 except (ValueError, AttributeError):
 ts = int(time.time())
 ELSE:
 ts = int(time.time())

 IF ts <= 0:
 ts = int(time.time())

 # Build output
 result = {
 "event_id": wr_id,
 "actor": {"type": "system", "id": agent_id},
 "intent": {
 "action": "execute",
 "target_type": "workrequest",
 "target_id": "workrequest:" + wr_id,
 },
 "domain": "execution",
 "timestamp": ts,
 "payload": {"data": {"work_request": dco}},
 }

 IF len(derived) > 0:
 result["causality"] = {"parent_event_ids": derived}

 # Postconditions:
 # All five required CCNF fields present
 # result["intent"]["action"] == "execute"
 # result["timestamp"] > 0
 # dco is not mutated

 RETURN result


### 
call_ccnf_conformance()


python
ALGORITHM call_ccnf_conformance(input_dict: dict, binary_path: str) -> dict:
 INPUT: input_dict — validated CCNF input document
 binary_path — path to ccnf-conformance executable
 OUTPUT: cer_json — CER dict with all 15 top-level fields

 IF binary_path does not exist OR is not executable:
 RAISE CCNFBridgeError("ccnf-conformance binary not found: {binary_path}")

 payload_bytes = json.dumps(input_dict).encode("utf-8")

 proc = subprocess.run(
 [binary_path, "run", "--version", "1"],
 input=payload_bytes,
 capture_output=True,
 timeout=CCNF_CONFORMANCE_TIMEOUT,
 )

 IF proc.returncode != 0:
 RAISE CCNFBridgeError(
 "ccnf-conformance exited {proc.returncode}: {proc.stderr[:500]}"
 )

 try:
 cer = json.loads(proc.stdout)
 except json.JSONDecodeError as e:
 RAISE CCNFBridgeError("ccnf-conformance output is not valid JSON: {e}")

 IF "signature" not in cer OR "hash" not in cer["signature"]:
 RAISE CCNFBridgeError("CER missing signature.hash")

 # Postconditions:
 # cer["signature"]["hash"] is a non-empty hex string
 # cer["event_id"] == input_dict["event_id"]

 RETURN cer


### 
deterministic_hash()


python
ALGORITHM deterministic_hash(cer_json: dict) -> str:
 INPUT: cer_json — CER dict returned by call_ccnf_conformance
 OUTPUT: hash_str — hex string (SHA256 of canonical CER bytes)

 sig = cer_json.get("signature") or {}
 h = sig.get("hash") or ""

 IF h == "":
 RAISE CCNFBridgeError("CER signature.hash is empty")

 # Postcondition: same cer_json always yields same h (CCNF I2 — idempotency)
 RETURN h


### 
CERBinder.attach_execution()


python
ALGORITHM CERBinder.attach_execution(...) -> dict:
 INPUT: cer_json, session_id, plan_id, wr_id, status, started_at, completed_at
 OUTPUT: receipt_dict

 # Preconditions:
 # wr_id is non-empty
 # started_at > 0, completed_at >= started_at
 # status in {"SUCCESS", "FAILURE", "PARTIAL"}

 ccnf_hash = deterministic_hash(cer_json)
 entity_key = cer_json["identity"]["entity_key"]
 duration_ms = (completed_at - started_at) * 1000

 IF status in ("SUCCESS", "PARTIAL"):
 replay_binding = _compute_replay_binding(entity_key, entity_key, 1, 1)
 trace_count = 1
 failure_node = None
 ELSE: # FAILURE
 replay_binding = ""
 trace_count = 0
 failure_node = {"code": "HARNESS_FAILURE", "message": "Harness exited with failure"}

 receipt = {
 "request_id": wr_id,
 "ccnf_hash": ccnf_hash,
 "cer_root_hash": entity_key,
 "trace_root_hash": entity_key,
 "trace_event_count": trace_count,
 "replay_binding_hash": replay_binding,
 "status": status,
 "failure": failure_node,
 "timing": {
 "started_at": started_at,
 "completed_at": completed_at,
 "duration_ms": duration_ms,
 },
 "ccnf_version": 1,
 }

 # Postconditions:
 # receipt["ccnf_hash"] == cer_json["signature"]["hash"]
 # receipt["timing"]["duration_ms"] >= 0
 # For SUCCESS: failure is None, replay_binding_hash != ""
 # For FAILURE: failure is non-None, trace_event_count == 0

 RETURN receipt

## Key Functions with Formal Specifications

### 
CCNFAdapter.from_work_request(dco_dict)


python
def from_work_request(dco_dict: dict) -> dict: ...


**Preconditions:**
- 
dco_dict
 is a non-None dict
- 
dco_dict["id"]
 is a non-empty string

**Postconditions:**
- Result contains keys: 
event_id
, 
actor
, 
intent
, 
domain
, 
timestamp

- 
result["intent"]["action"] == "execute"

- 
result["domain"] == "execution"

- 
result["timestamp"] > 0

- 
dco_dict
 is not mutated

### 
call_ccnf_conformance(input_dict, binary_path)


python
def call_ccnf_conformance(input_dict: dict, binary_path: str, ccnf_version: int = 1) -> dict: ...


**Preconditions:**
- 
input_dict
 has the five required CCNF top-level fields
- 
binary_path
 is a non-empty string

**Postconditions:**
- If binary succeeds: returns dict with 
signature.hash
 non-empty, 
event_id
 matching input
- If binary is absent or exits non-zero: raises 
CCNFBridgeError

- No filesystem writes

### 
deterministic_hash(cer_json)

def deterministic_hash(cer_json: dict) -> str: ...


**Preconditions:**
- 
cer_json["signature"]["hash"]
 is a non-empty hex string

**Postconditions:**
- Returns

- For identical 
cer_json

###

## Example Usage


python
import os, json, time
from ccnf_bridge import CCNFAdapter, CERBinder, call_ccnf_conformance, deterministic_hash

# --- Adapter: translate DCO to CCNF input ---
dco = {
 "id": "wr-abc123",
 "metadata": {"agent_id": "planner-1", "created_at": "2025-01-15T10:30:00Z"},
 "lineage": {"derived_from": ["wr-parent-001"]},
 # ... rest of DCO fields
}

ccnf_input = CCNFAdapter.from_work_request(dco)
assert ccnf_input["event_id"] == "wr-abc123"
assert ccnf_input["intent"]["action"] == "execute"
assert ccnf_input["domain"] == "execution"
assert ccnf_input["timestamp"] > 0

# --- Conformance call ---
binary = os.environ.get("CCNF_CONFORMANCE_BIN", "/path/to/bin/ccnf-conformance")
cer = call_ccnf_conformance(ccnf_input, binary)

# --- Hash extraction ---
ccnf_hash = deterministic_hash(cer)
assert len(ccnf_hash) == 64 # SHA256 hex

# --- Receipt assembly (after harness run) ---
started_at = int(time.time()) - 120
completed_at = int(time.time())

receipt = CERBinder.attach_execution(

)
assert receipt["ccnf_hash"] == ccnf_hash
assert receipt["request_id"] == "wr-abc123"
assert receipt["timing"]["duration_ms"] == (completed_at - started_at) * 1000

# Write to artifacts directory
with open("artifacts/wr-abc123/execution_receipt.json", "w") as f:

## Correctness Properties

The properties below can be verified with pytest + hypothesis.


python
# P1 — Feature flag isolation
# When CONDUIT_USE_CCNF is not set (or "false"), run_worker() behavior is unchanged.
# Testable by diffing result.json and exit codes between flag-on and flag-off runs
# on the same DCO.

# P2 — Adapter completeness
# For any valid DCO dict, from_work_request always returns a dict
# containing all five required CCNF top-level fields.
@given(dco=st.fixed_dictionaries({
 "id": st.text(min_size=1),
 "metadata": st.fixed_dictionaries({
 "agent_id": st.one_of(st.none(), st.text()),
 "created_at": st.one_of(st.none(), st.text()),
 }),
 "lineage": st.fixed_dictionaries({
 "derived_from": st.lists(st.text()),
 }),
}))
def test_adapter_always_has_required_fields(dco):
 result = CCNFAdapter.from_work_request(dco)
 assert all(k in result for k in ("event_id", "actor", "intent", "domain", "timestamp"))
 assert result["intent"]["action"] == "execute"
 assert result["domain"] == "execution"
 assert result["timestamp"] > 0

# P3 — Hash determinism
# Constructing the same DCO twice always yields the same ccnf_hash.
# Tested by calling from_work_request + deterministic_hash twice on identical input.
def test_deterministic_hash_same_dco():
 dco = build_test_dco("wr-fixed-id")
 h1 = deterministic_hash(call_ccnf_conformance(CCNFAdapter.from_work_request(dco), binary))
 h2 = deterministic_hash(call_ccnf_conformance(CCNFAdapter.from_work_request(dco), binary))
 assert h1 == h2

# P4 — Receipt ccnf_hash identity
# receipt["ccnf_hash"] always equals cer["signature"]["hash"].
def test_receipt_ccnf_hash_matches_cer_signature():
 cer = call_ccnf_conformance(ccnf_input, binary)
 receipt = CERBinder.attach_execution(cer, ..., status="SUCCESS", ...)
 assert receipt["ccnf_hash"] == cer["signature"]["hash"]

# P5 — Bridge failure fallback
# When binary is absent or exits non-zero, execution_receipt.json is NOT written
# and run_worker exits normally (0 for success, 3 for failure).
def test_bridge_fallback_on_missing_binary():
 run_worker_with_env({"CONDUIT_USE_CCNF": "true", "CCNF_CONFORMANCE_BIN": "/nonexistent"})
 assert not os.path.exists(artifacts_dir + "/execution_receipt.json")

# P6 — Receipt present on success
# When CONDUIT_USE_CCNF=true and binary succeeds, execution_receipt.json
# is present in the artifacts dir after run_worker() completes.
def test_receipt_written_on_success():
 run_worker_with_env({"CONDUIT_USE_CCNF": "true", "CCNF_CONFORMANCE_BIN": binary_path})
 assert os.path.exists(artifacts_dir + "/execution_receipt.json")
 receipt = json.load(open(artifacts_dir + "/execution_receipt.json"))
 assert receipt["request_id"] == wr_id
 assert len(receipt["ccnf_hash"]) == 64


---

## Error Handling

### Error Scenario 1: Binary not found

**Condition**: 
CONDUIT_USE_CCNF=true
 but 
CCNF_CONFORMANCE_BIN
 points to a
non-existent path (or 
ccnf-conformance
 is not on the default path).

**Response**: 
call_ccnf_conformance
 raises 
CCNFBridgeError
. The bridge exception
handler in 
run_worker()
 catches it, writes a 
[ccnf] WARNING
 line to the session log,
and sets 
_ccnf_cer_json = None
.

**Recovery**: Execution continues normally. No 
execution_receipt.json
 is written.

result.json
 and harness behavior are unchanged.

---

### Error Scenario 2: Binary exits non-zero

**Condition**: 
ccnf-conformance
 exits with a non-zero return code (e.g., input
validation failure, 
INTENT_NORMALIZATION_FAILURE
).

**Response**: Same as scenario 1 — 
CCNFBridgeError
 raised, warning logged,
execution continues.

**Recovery**: Same as scenario 1.

---

### Error Scenario 3: Malformed CER output

**Condition**: Binary exits 0 but stdout is not valid JSON, or 
signature.hash
 is absent.

**Response**: 
call_ccnf_conformance
 raises 
CCNFBridgeError
. Bridge falls back silently.

**Recovery**: Same as scenario 1.

---

### Error Scenario 4: Receipt write failure

**Condition**: 
execution_receipt.json
 cannot be written (permissions, disk full, etc.).

**Response**: 
_write_ccnf_receipt
 catches the exception, logs a warning, and returns
normally. The harness result and 
result.json
 are unaffected.

**Recovery**: 
run_worker()
 exits with the correct code regardless.

---

### Error Scenario 5: 
CONDUIT_USE_CCNF
 is not set or is 
"false"


**Condition**: Normal default operation.

**Response**: The bridge import block is never reached. No 
CCNFAdapter
,

call_ccnf_conformance
, or 
CERBinder
 code executes.

**Recovery**: N/A — this is the nominal path.

---

## Testing Strategy

### Unit Testing Approach

Each function in 
ccnf_bridge.py
 is independently unit-testable without a real

ccnf-conformance
 binary by injecting a mock subprocess result.

Key unit test cases:
- 
CCNFAdapter.from_work_request()
 with minimal DCO → check all five fields
- 
CCNFAdapter.from_work_request()
 with missing 
metadata.created_at
 → timestamp falls back to 
int(time.time())

- 
CCNFAdapter.from_work_request()
 with 
derived_from = []
 → no 
causality
 key in output
- 
CCNFAdapter.from_work_request()
 with 
derived_from = ["a","b"]
 → 
causality.parent_event_ids = ["a","b"]

- 
deterministic_hash()
 with valid CER → returns 
signature.hash

- 
deterministic_hash()
 with missing 
signature
 → raises 
CCNFBridgeError

- 
call_ccnf_conformance()
 with 
binary_path = "/nonexistent"
 → raises 
CCNFBridgeError

- 
call_ccnf_conformance()
 mocked non-zero exit → raises 
CCNFBridgeError

- 
call_ccnf_conformance()
 mocked invalid JSON stdout → raises 
CCNFBridgeError

- 
CERBinder.attach_execution()
 with 
status="SUCCESS"
 → 
failure is None
, 
replay_binding_hash != ""

- 
CERBinder.attach_execution()
 with 
status="FAILURE"
 → 
failure
 dict present, 
trace_event_count == 0


### Property-Based Testing Approach

**Property Test Library**: 
hypothesis


Key properties (see Correctness Properties section above):
- P2: Adapter completeness — 
from_work_request
 always returns a dict with all five required CCNF fields for any valid DCO
- P3: Hash determinism — same DCO always produces the same 
ccnf_hash
 (end-to-end with real binary)
- P4: 
receipt["ccnf_hash"] == cer["signature"]["hash"]
 for all valid CER outputs

### Integration Testing Approach

- Integration test invoking the real 
bin/ccnf-conformance
 binary with a synthesized
 DCO, asserting 
execution_receipt.json
 is written with a 64-character hex 
ccnf_hash

- Integration test with 
CONDUIT_USE_CCNF=false
 (or unset) against a real DCO,
 asserting 
execution_receipt.json
 is absent and 
result.json
 is identical to the
 pre-bridge baseline
- Integration test simulating binary timeout (mock subprocess) → receipt absent,
 executor exits cleanly

---

## Performance Considerations

The 
ccnf-conformance
 subprocess call is synchronous and adds latency to every

run_worker()
 invocation when 
CONDUIT_USE_CCNF=true
. Benchmarks on the reference
binary show sub-millisecond wall time for a single event normalization. The 30-second
timeout is a last-resort guard.

The entire bridge adds one subprocess call and one file write per 
run_worker()

invocation. No persistent connections, caching, or background threads are introduced.

---

## Security Considerations

- 
binary_path
 is resolved from an environment variable (
CCNF_CONFORMANCE_BIN
) or
 a relative default. It must not be user-controlled input passed in the DCO itself.
- The DCO dict is serialized to JSON and piped over stdin, not interpolated into a
 shell command string. No shell injection risk.
- The bridge does not transmit any data to external network endpoints.
- 
execution_receipt.json
 is written inside the existing 
artifacts_dir
 which is
 already scoped under the worker's working path. No path traversal is introduced.

---

## Dependencies

| Dependency | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| 
nexus/go/wrp/ccnf-ref/bin/ccnf-conformance
 | Runtime binary | Must be compiled; default path relative to repo root |
| 
subprocess
 | stdlib | Python 3.8+ |
| 
json
 | stdlib | |
| 
time
, 
datetime
 | stdlib | ISO-8601 parsing |
| 
os
 | stdlib | Binary existence check, env var read |
| 
pydantic
 | Already in conduit env | Not used directly by bridge; 
WorkRequestDCO
 lives in 
work_request.py
 |
| 
hypothesis
 | Test-only | Property-based tests |
| 
pytest
 | Test-only | Unit and integration tests |

No new third-party runtime dependencies are introduced.

# Design Document: ccnf-bridge

## Overview

The ccnf-bridge connects Conduit's existing 
WorkRequest
 execution pipeline to the CCNF
reference implementation (
ccnf-ref
). When the feature flag 
CONDUIT_USE_CCNF=true
 is set,

run_worker()
 invokes the 
ccnf-conformance
 binary after loading a DCO, records a CER
hash, and writes an 
ExecutionReceipt
 to the artifacts directory after harness completion.
When the flag is absent or false, 
run_worker()
 behavior is byte-for-byte unchanged.

The bridge is contained in one new file (
nexus/python/conduit/ccnf_bridge.py
) and a
minimal insertion into 
run_worker()
 in the existing 
executor_cloud.py
. No other
Conduit code is modified.

---

## Architecture


mermaid
graph TD
 A[run_worker - executor_cloud.py] -->|CONDUIT_USE_CCNF=true| B[CCNFAdapter.from_work_request]
 B --> C[call_ccnf_conformance - subprocess]
 C -->|stdin: CCNF JSON| D[bin/ccnf-conformance]
 D -->|stdout: CER JSON| C
 C --> E[deterministic_hash - extracts cer.signature.hash]
 E --> F[store cer_json + ccnf_hash in-memory]
 A -->|after harness completion| G[CERBinder.attach_execution]
 F --> G
 G --> H[write execution_receipt.json to artifacts_dir]

 A -->|CONDUIT_USE_CCNF=false| I[unchanged existing path]
 C -->|binary absent or non-zero exit| J[warn to session log, continue without CCNF]


mermaid
sequenceDiagram
 participant W as run_worker
 participant B as CCNFBridge
 participant X as ccnf-conformance binary
 participant FS as Filesystem

 W->>W: json.load(request_path) → req
 W->>B: CCNFAdapter.from_work_request(req) → ccnf_input
 W->>B: call_ccnf_conformance(ccnf_input, binary_path) → cer_json
 B->>X: subprocess stdin: ccnf_input JSON
 X-->>B: stdout: CER JSON
 B->>W: cer_json (dict)
 W->>B: deterministic_hash(cer_json) → ccnf_hash
 W->>W: store (cer_json, ccnf_hash) locally
 W->>W: resolve harness + model, run DAG / fast-path
 W->>B: CERBinder.attach_execution(cer_json, session_id, plan_id, wr_id) → receipt_dict
 W->>FS: write artifacts_dir/execution_receipt.json
 W->>W: exit(0 or 3)


---

## Components and Interfaces

### Component 1: 
CCNFAdapter


**Purpose**: Translate a raw 
WorkRequestDCO
 dict into the JSON object that

ccnf.Run()
 / 
ccnf-conformance
 expects.

**Interface**:


python
class CCNFAdapter:
 @staticmethod
 def from_work_request(dco_dict: dict) -> dict:
 """
 Translate a WorkRequestDCO dict into a CCNF input document.

 Preconditions:
 - dco_dict is a non-None dict
 - dco_dict["id"] exists and is a non-empty string
 - dco_dict["metadata"]["created_at"] is an ISO-8601 string or None

 Postconditions:
 - Returns a dict containing all five required top-level keys:
 "event_id", "actor", "intent", "domain", "timestamp"
 - "intent.action" is always "execute" (controlled vocabulary)
 - "domain" is always "execution"
 - "timestamp" is an int64 epoch seconds value > 0
 - "causality.parent_event_ids" contains dco_dict["lineage"]["derived_from"]
 if that list is non-empty; the key is omitted if empty
 - "payload.data.work_request" contains the full dco_dict

 No side effects on dco_dict.
 """


**Field mapping**:

| DCO field | CCNF input field | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| 
dco["id"]
 | 
event_id
 | Direct copy |
| 
"system"
 | 
actor.type
 | Hardcoded literal |
| 
dco["metadata"]["agent_id"]
 or 
"conduit"
 | 
actor.id
 | Falls back to 
"conduit"
 |
| 
"execute"
 | 
intent.action
 | Controlled vocabulary |
| 
"workrequest"
 | 
intent.target_type
 | Hardcoded literal |
| 
"workrequest:" + dco["id"]
 | 
intent.target_id
 | Composite |
| 
"execution"
 | 
domain
 | Hardcoded literal |
| 
dco["metadata"]["created_at"]
 → epoch int | 
timestamp
 | ISO-8601 parsed; fallback 
int(time.time())
 |
| 
dco["lineage"]["derived_from"]
 | 
causality.parent_event_ids
 | Omitted if empty list |
| 
dco
 (full dict) | 
payload.data.work_request
 | Nested under 
payload.data
 |

**Responsibilities**:
- Parse 
created_at
 ISO-8601 string to epoch seconds (handles missing/malformed gracefully)
- Never mutate the input dict
- Always return a dict with the five required CCNF top-level fields

---

### Component 2: 
call_ccnf_conformance


**Purpose**: Invoke the 
ccnf-conformance
 binary as a subprocess, feed the CCNF input
over stdin, and return the parsed CER JSON dict.

**Interface**:


python
def call_ccnf_conformance(
 input_dict: dict,
 binary_path: str,
 ccnf_version: int = 1,
) -> dict:
 """
 Invoke the ccnf-conformance binary and return the parsed CER JSON.

 Preconditions:
 - input_dict is a valid CCNF input document (has event_id, actor, intent, domain, timestamp)
 - binary_path points to the ccnf-conformance executable

 Postconditions:
 - Returns a dict representing the CER (all 15 top-level fields present)
 - Raises CCNFBridgeError if:
 - binary is not found (FileNotFoundError)
 - binary exits non-zero
 - stdout is not valid JSON
 - parsed dict does not contain "signature" → "hash"

 Side effects: subprocess execution only; no filesystem writes.
 """


**Subprocess protocol**:
- Command: 
[binary_path, "run", "--version", str(ccnf_version)]

- Input: 
json.dumps(input_dict)
 piped to stdin
- Output: CER JSON on stdout
- Timeout: 30 seconds (configurable via 
CCNF_CONFORMANCE_TIMEOUT
 env var)
- Non-zero exit → raises 
CCNFBridgeError


---

### Component 3: 
deterministic_hash


**Purpose**: Extract the canonical hash from a CER JSON dict.

**Interface**:


python
def deterministic_hash(cer_json: dict) -> str:
 """
 Extract cer["signature"]["hash"] from a parsed CER dicso where t.

 Preconditions:
 - cer_json is a dict
 - cer_json["signature"]["hash"] is a non-empty string

 Postconditions:
 - Returns cer_json["signature"]["hash"] unchanged
 - The returned value is identical for identical input dicts
 (determinism inherited from CCNF pipeline)
 - Raises CCNFBridgeError if the hash field is absent or empty

 No side effects.
 """


---

### Component 4: 
CERBinder


**Purpose**: Build an 
ExecutionReceipt
-shaped dict from the CER output and execution
context, ready for JSON serialization.

**Interface**:


python
class CERBinder:
 @staticmethod
 def attach_execution(
 cer_json: dict,
 session_id: str,
 plan_id: str,
 wr_id: str,
 status: str, # "SUCCESS" | "FAILURE" | "PARTIAL"
 started_at: int, # epoch seconds
 completed_at: int, # epoch seconds
 failure_code: str | None = None,
 failure_message: str | None = None,
 ) -> dict:
 """
 Build an ExecutionReceipt dict from CER output.

 Preconditions:
 - cer_json contains "signature" → "hash"
 - wr_id is non-empty
 - started_at > 0, completed_at >= started_at
 - status is one of "SUCCESS", "FAILURE", "PARTIAL"

 Postconditions:
 - Returns a dict with fields matching ExecutionReceipt (runtime/types.go):
 request_id, ccnf_hash, cer_root_hash, trace_root_hash,
 trace_event_count, replay_binding_hash, status, timing, ccnf_version
 - "ccnf_hash" equals deterministic_hash(cer_json)
 - "request_id" equals wr_id
 - "timing.duration_ms" equals (completed_at - started_at) * 1000
 - For SUCCESS/PARTIAL: replay_binding_hash is non-empty;
 for FAILURE: failure node is present

 No side effects.
 """


**Field mapping to 
ExecutionReceipt
**:

| Python value | Receipt field | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| 
wr_id
 | 
request_id
 | Direct |
| 
deterministic_hash(cer_json)

ccnf_hash
 | Must match exactly |
| 
cer_json["identity"]["entity_key"]
 | 
cer_root_hash
 | SHA256-derived |
| 
cer_json["identity"]["entity_key"]
 | 
trace_root_hash
 | Same value in v1 |
| 
1
 | 
trace_event_count
 | Single-event bridge (v1) |
| 
_compute_replay_binding(...)
 | 
replay_binding_hash
 | domain-sep hash for SUCCESS/PARTIAL |
| 
status
 | 
status
 | 
"SUCCESS"
 \| 
"FAILURE"
 \| 
"PARTIAL"
 |
| 
started_at
, 
completed_at
 | 
timing

duration_ms = (completed_at - started_at) * 1000
 |
| 
1
 | 
ccnf_version
 | Hardcoded v1 |

---

### Component 5: 
run_worker()
 insertion (executor_cloud.py)

**Purpose**: Graft the bridge into the existing worker without changing any non-CCNF paths.

**Insertion point 1** — after 
req = json.load(f)
, before

**Insertion point 2** — before every 
exit(0)

a shared helper called once after harness completion:


python
def _write_ccnf_receipt(
 artifacts_dir: str | None,
 cer_json: dict | None,
 wr_id: str,
 session_id: str,

) -> None:
 """Write ExecutionReceipt to artifacts_dir if CCNF bridge ran successfully."""
 if not artifacts_dir or not cer_json or not started_at:
 return

 import time as _time
 completed_at = int(_time.time())
 status_str = "SUCCESS" if success else "FAILURE"

 )

 _write_session_log(session_log_path, f"[ccnf] receipt written: {receipt_path}\n")
 except Exception as _e:
 _write_session_log(session_log_path, f"[ccnf] WARNING: receipt write failed: {_e}\n")


This helper is called before every exit point that currently calls 
_write_result_event
.

---

## Data Models

### Model 1: CCNF Input Document

Produced by 
CCNFAdapter.from_work_request()
. Subset of the full CCNF input schema
(
ccnf-ref/spec/CCNF_SPEC.md §9.2
).


python
ccnf_input = {
 # Required by CCNF pipeline
 "event_id": str, # non-empty
 "actor": {
 "type": "system",
 "id": str, # agent_id or "conduit"
 },
 "intent": {
 "action": "execute", # controlled vocabulary
 "target_type": "workrequest",
 "target_id": "workrequest:<wr_id>",
 },
 "domain": "execution",
 "timestamp": int, # epoch seconds, > 0

 # Optional
 "causality": {
 "parent_event_ids": list[str], # may be omitted if empty
 },
 "payload": {
 "data": {
 "work_request": dict, # full DCO
 }
 },
}


**Validation rules**:
- 
event_id
 must be non-empty
- 
actor.id
 must be a non-empty string
- 
intent.action
 must be exactly 
"execute"

- 
timestamp
 must be a positive integer

### Model 2: ExecutionReceipt dict (Python-side representation)

Written to 
artifacts_dir/execution_receipt.json
. Mirrors 
runtime.ExecutionReceipt

from 
runtime/types.go
.


python
receipt = {
 "request_id": str, # wr_id
 "ccnf_hash": str, # cer["signature"]["hash"]
 "cer_root_hash": str, # cer["identity"]["entity_key"]
 "trace_root_hash": str, # cer["identity"]["entity_key"] (v1)
 "trace_event_count": int, # 1 (single-event bridge)
 "replay_binding_hash": str, # domain-separated hash (SUCCESS/PARTIAL)
 "status": str, # "SUCCESS" | "FAILURE" | "PARTIAL"
 "failure": dict | None, # {code, message} or None
 "timing": {
 "started_at": int, # epoch seconds
 "completed_at": int, # epoch seconds
 "duration_ms": int, # (completed_at - started_at) * 1000
 },
 "ccnf_version": 1,
}


**Validation rules** (mirrors 
ValidateReceipt
 in 
runtime/validator.go
):
- 
request_id
 must be non-empty
- 
timing.duration_ms
 must be ≥ 0
- For 
"SUCCESS"
: 
ccnf_hash
, 
trace_root_hash
, 
replay_binding_hash
 non-empty;
 
trace_event_count
 > 0; 
failure
 is 
None

- For 
"FAILURE"
: 
failure
 is non-None; 
trace_event_count
 is 0
- For 
"PARTIAL"
: 
failure

### Model 3: 
CCNFBridgeError


python
class CCNFBridgeError(RuntimeError):
 """Raised when the CCNF bridge cannot complete normally.

 Callers catch this and fall back to the non-CCNF path.
 """

## Algorithmic Pseudocode

### Main Bridge Flow in 
run_worker()


python
ALGORITHM run_worker_with_ccnf_bridge(request_path):
 INPUT: request_path: str
 OUTPUT: side effects only (writes to disk, exits with code 0 or 3)

 # Precondition: request_path is a valid path to a DCO JSON file
 req = json.load(open(request_path))

 # Bridge insertion point 1
 cer_json, ccnf_hash, started_at = None, None, None
 if CONDUIT_USE_CCNF is enabled:
 ccnf_input = CCNFAdapter.from_work_request(req)
 ASSERT "event_id" in ccnf_input
 ASSERT "actor" in ccnf_input
 ASSERT "intent" in ccnf_input
 ASSERT ccnf_input["domain"] == "execution"
 ASSERT ccnf_input["timestamp"] > 0
 try:
 cer_json = call_ccnf_conformance(ccnf_input, binary_path)
 ccnf_hash = deterministic_hash(cer_json)
 started_at = now()
 log("[ccnf] anchored wr={wr_id} hash={ccnf_hash}")
 except any exception:
 log("[ccnf] WARNING: bridge failed, continuing")
 cer_json, ccnf_hash, started_at = None, None, None

 # Existing execution path (unchanged)
 run harness or DAG steps → success_flag

 # Bridge insertion point 2 (before exit)
 if cer_json is not None AND started_at is not None:
 receipt = CERBinder.attach_execution(
 cer_json, session_id, "", wr_id,
 "SUCCESS" if success_flag else "FAILURE",
 started_at, now()
 )
 write receipt to artifacts_dir/execution_receipt.json
 # On write failure: log warning, do NOT propagate exception

 exit(0 if success_flag else 3)
 # Postcondition: execution_receipt.json exists iff CCNF bridge succeeded


### 
CCNFAdapter.from_work_request()


python
ALGORITHM CCNFAdapter.from_work_request(dco: dict) -> dict:
 INPUT: dco — WorkRequestDCO dict (raw JSON)
 OUTPUT: ccnf_input — CCNF input document dict

 # Preconditions:
 # dco["id"] is non-empty string
 # dco["metadata"]["created_at"] is ISO-8601 or None

 wr_id = dco["id"]
 meta = dco.get("metadata") or {}
 agent_id = meta.get("agent_id") or "conduit"
 lineage = dco.get("lineage") or {}
 derived = lineage.get("derived_from") or []

 # Timestamp parsing
 created_at_str = meta.get("created_at")
 IF created_at_str is not None:
 try:
 ts = int(datetime.fromisoformat(created_at_str.replace("Z", "+00:00")).timestamp())
 except (ValueError, AttributeError):
 ts = int(time.time())
 ELSE:
 ts = int(time.time())

 IF ts <= 0:
 ts = int(time.time())

 # Build output
 result = {
 "event_id": wr_id,
 "actor": {"type": "system", "id": agent_id},
 "intent": {
 "action": "execute",
 "target_type": "workrequest",
 "target_id": "workrequest:" + wr_id,
 },
 "domain": "execution",
 "timestamp": ts,
 "payload": {"data": {"work_request": dco}},
 }

 IF len(derived) > 0:
 result["causality"] = {"parent_event_ids": derived}

 # Postconditions:
 # All five required CCNF fields present
 # result["intent"]["action"] == "execute"
 # result["timestamp"] > 0
 # dco is not mutated

 RETURN result


### 
call_ccnf_conformance()


python
ALGORITHM call_ccnf_conformance(input_dict: dict, binary_path: str) -> dict:
 INPUT: input_dict — validated CCNF input document
 binary_path — path to ccnf-conformance executable
 OUTPUT: cer_json — CER dict with all 15 top-level fields

 IF binary_path does not exist OR is not executable:
 RAISE CCNFBridgeError("ccnf-conformance binary not found: {binary_path}")

 payload_bytes = json.dumps(input_dict).encode("utf-8")

 proc = subprocess.run(
 [binary_path, "run", "--version", "1"],
 input=payload_bytes,
 capture_output=True,
 timeout=CCNF_CONFORMANCE_TIMEOUT,
 )

 IF proc.returncode != 0:
 RAISE CCNFBridgeError(
 "ccnf-conformance exited {proc.returncode}: {proc.stderr[:500]}"
 )

 try:
 cer = json.loads(proc.stdout)
 except json.JSONDecodeError as e:
 RAISE CCNFBridgeError("ccnf-conformance output is not valid JSON: {e}")

 IF "signature" not in cer OR "hash" not in cer["signature"]:
 RAISE CCNFBridgeError("CER missing signature.hash")

 # Postconditions:
 # cer["signature"]["hash"] is a non-empty hex string
 # cer["event_id"] == input_dict["event_id"]

 RETURN cer


### 
deterministic_hash()


python
ALGORITHM deterministic_hash(cer_json: dict) -> str:
 INPUT: cer_json — CER dict returned by call_ccnf_conformance
 OUTPUT: hash_str — hex string (SHA256 of canonical CER bytes)

 sig = cer_json.get("signature") or {}
 h = sig.get("hash") or ""

 IF h == "":
 RAISE CCNFBridgeError("CER signature.hash is empty")

 # Postcondition: same cer_json always yields same h (CCNF I2 — idempotency)
 RETURN h


### 
CERBinder.attach_execution()


python
ALGORITHM CERBinder.attach_execution(...) -> dict:
 INPUT: cer_json, session_id, plan_id, wr_id, status, started_at, completed_at
 OUTPUT: receipt_dict

 # Preconditions:
 # wr_id is non-empty
 # started_at > 0, completed_at >= started_at
 # status in {"SUCCESS", "FAILURE", "PARTIAL"}

 ccnf_hash = deterministic_hash(cer_json)
 entity_key = cer_json["identity"]["entity_key"]
 duration_ms = (completed_at - started_at) * 1000

 IF status in ("SUCCESS", "PARTIAL"):
 replay_binding = _compute_replay_binding(entity_key, entity_key, 1, 1)
 trace_count = 1
 failure_node = None
 ELSE: # FAILURE
 replay_binding = ""
 trace_count = 0
 failure_node = {"code": "HARNESS_FAILURE", "message": "Harness exited with failure"}

 receipt = {
 "request_id": wr_id,
 "ccnf_hash": ccnf_hash,
 "cer_root_hash": entity_key,
 "trace_root_hash": entity_key,
 "trace_event_count": trace_count,
 "replay_binding_hash": replay_binding,
 "status": status,
 "failure": failure_node,
 "timing": {
 "started_at": started_at,
 "completed_at": completed_at,
 "duration_ms": duration_ms,
 },
 "ccnf_version": 1,
 }

 # Postconditions:
 # receipt["ccnf_hash"] == cer_json["signature"]["hash"]
 # receipt["timing"]["duration_ms"] >= 0
 # For SUCCESS: failure is None, replay_binding_hash != ""
 # For FAILURE: failure is non-None, trace_event_count == 0

 RETURN receipt

## Example Usage


python
import os, json, time
from ccnf_bridge import CCNFAdapter, CERBinder, call_ccnf_conformance, deterministic_hash

# --- Adapter: translate DCO to CCNF input ---
dco = {
 "id": "wr-abc123",
 "metadata": {"agent_id": "planner-1", "created_at": "2025-01-15T10:30:00Z"},
 "lineage": {"derived_from": ["wr-parent-001"]},
 # ... rest of DCO fields
}

ccnf_input = CCNFAdapter.from_work_request(dco)
assert ccnf_input["event_id"] == "wr-abc123"
assert ccnf_input["intent"]["action"] == "execute"
assert ccnf_input["domain"] == "execution"
assert ccnf_input["timestamp"] > 0

# --- Conformance call ---
binary = os.environ.get("CCNF_CONFORMANCE_BIN", "/path/to/bin/ccnf-conformance")
cer = call_ccnf_conformance(ccnf_input, binary)

# --- Hash extraction ---

assert len(ccnf_hash) == 64 # SHA256 hex

# --- Receipt assembly (after harness run) ---
started_at = int(time.time()) - 120
completed_at = int(time.time())

receipt = CERBinder.attach_execution(

)
assert receipt["ccnf_hash"] == ccnf_hash
assert receipt["request_id"] == "wr-abc123"
assert receipt["timing"]["duration_ms"] == (completed_at - started_at) * 1000

# Write to artifacts directory
with open("artifacts/wr-abc123/execution_receipt.json", "w") as f:

## Correctness Properties

The properties below can be verified with pytest + hypothesis.


python
# P1 — Feature flag isolation
# When CONDUIT_USE_CCNF is not set (or "false"), run_worker() behavior is unchanged.
# Testable by diffing result.json and exit codes between flag-on and flag-off runs
# on the same DCO.

# P2 — Adapter completeness
# For any valid DCO dict, from_work_request always returns a dict
# containing all five required CCNF top-level fields.
@given(dco=st.fixed_dictionaries({
 "id": st.text(min_size=1),
 "metadata": st.fixed_dictionaries({
 "agent_id": st.one_of(st.none(), st.text()),
 "created_at": st.one_of(st.none(), st.text()),
 }),
 "lineage": st.fixed_dictionaries({
 "derived_from": st.lists(st.text()),
 }),
}))
def test_adapter_always_has_required_fields(dco):
 result = CCNFAdapter.from_work_request(dco)
 assert all(k in result for k in ("event_id", "actor", "intent", "domain", "timestamp"))
 assert result["intent"]["action"] == "execute"
 assert result["domain"] == "execution"
 assert result["timestamp"] > 0

# P3 — Hash determinism
# Constructing the same DCO twice always yields the same ccnf_hash.
# Tested by calling from_work_request + deterministic_hash twice on identical input.
def test_deterministic_hash_same_dco():
 dco = build_test_dco("wr-fixed-id")
 h1 = deterministic_hash(call_ccnf_conformance(CCNFAdapter.from_work_request(dco), binary))
 h2 = deterministic_hash(call_ccnf_conformance(CCNFAdapter.from_work_request(dco), binary))
 assert h1 == h2

# P4 — Receipt ccnf_hash identity
# receipt["ccnf_hash"] always equals cer["signature"]["hash"].
def test_receipt_ccnf_hash_matches_cer_signature():
 cer = call_ccnf_conformance(ccnf_input, binary)
 receipt = CERBinder.attach_execution(cer, ..., status="SUCCESS", ...)
 assert receipt["ccnf_hash"] == cer["signature"]["hash"]

# P5 — Bridge failure fallback
# When binary is absent or exits non-zero, execution_receipt.json is NOT written
# and run_worker exits normally (0 for success, 3 for failure).
def test_bridge_fallback_on_missing_binary():
 run_worker_with_env({"CONDUIT_USE_CCNF": "true", "CCNF_CONFORMANCE_BIN": "/nonexistent"})
 assert not os.path.exists(artifacts_dir + "/execution_receipt.json")

# P6 — Receipt present on success
# When CONDUIT_USE_CCNF=true and binary succeeds, execution_receipt.json
# is present in the artifacts dir after run_worker() completes.
def test_receipt_written_on_success():
 run_worker_with_env({"CONDUIT_USE_CCNF": "true", "CCNF_CONFORMANCE_BIN": binary_path})
 assert os.path.exists(artifacts_dir + "/execution_receipt.json")
 receipt = json.load(open(artifacts_dir + "/execution_receipt.json"))
 assert receipt["request_id"] == wr_id
 assert len(receipt["ccnf_hash"]) == 64


---

## Error Handling

### Error Scenario 1: Binary not found

**Condition**: 
CONDUIT_USE_CCNF=true
 but 
CCNF_CONFORMANCE_BIN
 points to a
non-existent path (or 
ccnf-conformance
 is not on the default path).

**Response**: 
call_ccnf_conformance
 raises 
CCNFBridgeError
. The bridge exception
handler in 
run_worker()
 catches it, writes a 
[ccnf] WARNING
 line to the session log,
and sets 
_ccnf_cer_json = None
.

**Recovery**: Execution continues normally. No 
execution_receipt.json
 is written.

result.json
 and harness behavior are unchanged.

---

### Error Scenario 2: Binary exits non-zero

**Condition**: 
ccnf-conformance
 exits with a non-zero return code (e.g., input
validation failure, 
INTENT_NORMALIZATION_FAILURE
).

**Response**: Same as scenario 1 — 
CCNFBridgeError
 raised, warning logged,
execution continues.

**Recovery**: Same as scenario 1.

---

### Error Scenario 3: Malformed CER output

**Condition**: Binary exits 0 but stdout is not valid JSON, or 
signature.hash
 is absent.

**Response**: 
call_ccnf_conformance
 raises 
CCNFBridgeError
. Bridge falls back silently.

**Recovery**: Same as scenario 1.

---

### Error Scenario 4: Receipt write failure

**Condition**: 
execution_receipt.json
 cannot be written (permissions, disk full, etc.).

**Response**: 
_write_ccnf_receipt
 catches the exception, logs a warning, and returns
normally. The harness result and 
result.json
 are unaffected.

**Recovery**: 
run_worker()
 exits with the correct code regardless.

---

### Error Scenario 5: 
CONDUIT_USE_CCNF
 is not set or is 
"false"


**Condition**: Normal default operation.

**Response**: The bridge import block is never reached. No 
CCNFAdapter
,

call_ccnf_conformance
, or 
CERBinder
 code executes.

**Recovery**: N/A — this is the nominal path.

---

## Testing Strategy

### Unit Testing Approach

Each function in 
ccnf_bridge.py
 is independently unit-testable without a real

ccnf-conformance
 binary by injecting a mock subprocess result.

Key unit test cases:
- 
CCNFAdapter.from_work_request()
 with minimal DCO → check all five fields
- 
CCNFAdapter.from_work_request()
 with missing 
metadata.created_at
 → timestamp falls back to 
int(time.time())

- 
CCNFAdapter.from_work_request()
 with 
derived_from = []
 → no 
causality
 key in output
- 
CCNFAdapter.from_work_request()
 with 
derived_from = ["a","b"]
 → 
causality.parent_event_ids = ["a","b"]

- 
deterministic_hash()
 with valid CER → returns 
signature.hash

- 
deterministic_hash()
 with missing 
signature
 → raises 
CCNFBridgeError

- 
call_ccnf_conformance()
 with 
binary_path = "/nonexistent"
 → raises 
CCNFBridgeError

- 
call_ccnf_conformance()
 mocked non-zero exit → raises 
CCNFBridgeError

- 
call_ccnf_conformance()
 mocked invalid JSON stdout → raises 
CCNFBridgeError

- 
CERBinder.attach_execution()
 with 
status="SUCCESS"
 → 
failure is None
, 
replay_binding_hash != ""

- 
CERBinder.attach_execution()
 with 
status="FAILURE"
 → 
failure
 dict present, 
trace_event_count == 0


### Property-Based Testing Approach

**Property Test Library**: 
hypothesis


Key properties (see Correctness Properties section above):
- P2: Adapter completeness — 
from_work_request
 always returns a dict with all five required CCNF fields for any valid DCO
- P3: Hash determinism — same DCO always produces the same 
ccnf_hash
 (end-to-end with real binary)
- P4: 
receipt["ccnf_hash"] == cer["signature"]["hash"]
 for all valid CER outputs

### Integration Testing Approach

- Integration test invoking the real 
bin/ccnf-conformance
 binary with a synthesized
 DCO, asserting 
execution_receipt.json
 is written with a 64-character hex 
ccnf_hash

- Integration test with 
CONDUIT_USE_CCNF=false
 (or unset) against a real DCO,
 asserting 
execution_receipt.json
 is absent and 
result.json
 is identical to the
 pre-bridge baseline
- Integration test simulating binary timeout (mock subprocess) → receipt absent,
 executor exits cleanly

---

## Performance Considerations

The 
ccnf-conformance
 subprocess call is synchronous and adds latency to every

run_worker()
 invocation when 
CONDUIT_USE_CCNF=true
. Benchmarks on the reference
binary show sub-millisecond wall time for a single event normalization. The 30-second
timeout is a last-resort guard.

The entire bridge adds one subprocess call and one file write per 
run_worker()

invocation. No persistent connections, caching, or background threads are introduced.

---

## Security Considerations

- 
binary_path
 is resolved from an environment variable (
CCNF_CONFORMANCE_BIN
) or
 a relative default. It must not be user-controlled input passed in the DCO itself.
- The DCO dict is serialized to JSON and piped over stdin, not interpolated into a
 shell command string. No shell injection risk.
- The bridge does not transmit any data to external network endpoints.
- 
execution_receipt.json
 is written inside the existing 
artifacts_dir
 which is
 already scoped under the worker's working path. No path traversal is introduced.

---

## Dependencies

| Dependency | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| 
nexus/go/wrp/ccnf-ref/bin/ccnf-conformance
 | Runtime binary | Must be compiled; default path relative to repo root |
| 
subprocess
 | stdlib | Python 3.8+ |
| 
json
 | stdlib | |
| 
time
, 
datetime
 | stdlib | ISO-8601 parsing |
| 
os
 | stdlib | Binary existence check, env var read |
| 
pydantic
 | Already in conduit env | Not used directly by bridge; 
WorkRequestDCO
 lives in 
work_request.py
 |
| 
hypothesis
 | Test-only | Property-based tests |
| 
pytest
 | Test-only | Unit and integration tests |

No new third-party runtime dependencies are introduced.

discourse_units.heading: Turn 3 — assistant
discourse_units.body:
This is actually already 
much closer to a real load-bearing bridge
 than most “integration layers” people write. It has three properties that matter a lot in your system:
- Feature-flag isolation is clean
- Failure is explicitly non-fatal
- The CCNF artifact is treated as a side-channel, not the primary execution path
That combination is exactly what makes it safe to introduce something “foundational-adjacent” without destabilizing Conduit.
But there are a few subtle architectural tensions here that are worth calling out before you move on, because they affect whether CCNF-bridge becomes 
just plumbing
 or becomes part of your future “self-gap detection” layer.
Right now you have:
WorkRequest → run_worker → harness/DAG → ExecutionReceipt (existing system)
WorkRequest → CCNFAdapter → ccnf-conformance → CER → CERBinder → ExecutionReceipt augmentation
That means:
> You now have two independent “truth derivation paths” converging into one receipt artifact.
That is powerful, but it creates a latent question:
Right now the answer is implicitly:
> “CCNF is observational, not authoritative”
But you haven’t encoded that invariant anywhere.
You have:
- CCNF runs “if available”
- failure is swallowed
- execution continues unchanged
But you do NOT yet have a formal system rule like:
> “CCNF must never influence execution outcome in v1”
That sounds obvious, but in systems like yours, it matters because later you will inevitably want:
- policy gating
- execution veto
- structural enforcement
If CCNF is not explicitly declared as:
> observational-only bridge layer
then later upgrades will be ambiguous and risky.
This is the important part.
Your bridge is not just:
> Conduit → external binary
It is actually defining:
> Canonicalization boundary between DCO semantics and CCNF event semantics
That means CCNFAdapter is doing something more important than “mapping fields”:
It is defining:
> what Conduit
means
when it says “execute”
That’s not implementation glue—that’s ontology alignment.
Right now that ontology is implicit. You’re one step away from making it explicit.
This is the part that will matter later for your “gap detection” goal.
Your adapter guarantees:
- required fields exist in CCNF input
But it does NOT define:
> what information is
not representable
in CCNF
That’s the real bridge intelligence.
Because later your system will need to answer:
- “what did we lose when translating this WorkRequest into CCNF?”
- “what CCNF cannot express from our internal model?”
- “what assumptions were injected?”
Right now that information disappears silently.
So CCNF-bridge is:
- deterministic ✔
- stable ✔
- but not yet introspective ✖
This line is actually doing more than it looks like:
> ccnf_hash = deterministic_hash(cer_json)
Because that creates:
- a stable identity for external conformance output
- a reference point for future replay/debug/verification
This is exactly the kind of thing your future “audit + gap detection layer” will build on.
If you zoom out, CCNF-bridge is evolving into one of these:
> External validation plugin
> Semantic projection layer between internal execution model and canonical event theory
> First-class “interpretation axis” of the system (used for gap detection, policy reasoning, and structural introspection)
Right now you’re sitting between A and B.
If you do only one refinement before moving on:
Right now everything collapses into 
ExecutionReceipt
.
But what you actually want long-term is:
- ExecutionReceipt = what happened
- CCNFReport = what CCNF believes happened
So something like:
```
ccnf_report
.
json
```
Containing:
- input hash (DCO hash)

smart but ungoverned
, which in your architecture would eventually turn into silent structural drift.
So we do:
> Governance first → then prediction
This layer sits 
between GapCompiler and WorkRequest execution
.
Its job is simple in principle but strict in effect:
> “Nothing generated by the system is allowed to mutate the system without passing policy gates.”
Governance is NOT optional in your system.
It is a 
hard boundary
.
We introduce a new object:
```
GovernanceDecision
 {
    
intent_id
: 
str
,

:

"system | policy | human"
,
}
```
Each RepairIntent must pass three gates:
> “Can this change damage system invariants?”
Reject if:
- modifies execution kernel behavior
- removes observability hooks
- alters identity or hashing rules
- affects multiple layers simultaneously
> “Is this change local and minimal?”
Reject if:
- touches more than one subsystem
- lacks clear target file/module/layer
- is ambiguous in effect boundary
> “Can this change be undone cleanly?”
Reject if:
- schema migration without rollback strategy
- stateful irreversible transformation
- identity system changes without versioning
We formalize:
```
def
 
governance_score
(
intent
: 
RepairIntent
) -> 
float
:
    
risk
 
=
 
0
    
if
 
intent
.
type 
in
 
CRITICAL_SYSTEM_TYPES
:
        
risk
 
+=
 
0.5

intent
.

 [
"kernel"
, 
"identity"
, 
"execution"
]:

+=
 
0.3

intent
.
risk_level 
==
 
"high"
:

+=
 
0.2
    
if
 
not
 
intent
.

.

"reversible"
, 
True

0.3

min
(

, 
risk
)
```
```
0.0 – 0.3 → APPROVE
0.3 – 0.6 → MODIFY
0.6 – 0.8 → DEFER
0.8 – 1.0 → REJECT
```
This is where intelligence enters governance.
Instead of rejecting, the system can:
- reduce scope
- split WorkRequest
- require observability hooks
- force explicit rollback plan
Example:
> “This ontology extension is too broad → split into 3 WorkRequests”
This prevents:
- monolithic self-patching
- hidden architectural drift
- uncontrolled abstraction jumps
Every decision emits:
```
GovernanceEvent
 {

: 
str
,

:

,

,

: 
float

[
str
]
}
```
This matters because:
> governance itself becomes observable and auditable
No hidden policy logic.
Even in fully autonomous mode, you keep:
- APPROVE overrides
- REJECT overrides
But critically:
> overrides are also recorded as events
So governance is never bypassed, only overridden explicitly.
These are system-level guarantees:
Everything must pass governance.
Even CCNF failure paths cannot auto-approve.
It only produces decisions.
No hidden learning inside this layer (learning comes later in B)
This is the key shift:
Before:
> system generates repairs → executes them
After:
> system generates repairs → evaluates risk → constrains itself → executes safely
This prevents:
- runaway self-modification loops
- ontology explosion
- silent schema drift
You said:
> B is more interesting
It is—but here’s the catch:
Without governance, predictive modeling becomes dangerous because:
> the system begins predicting
and acting on its own predictions
That leads to:
- self-fulfilling structural changes
- reinforcement of bad abstractions
- feedback loops that look “intelligent” but are actually unstable
Governance gives you:
> clean labeled history of what was safe vs unsafe to change
That is essential training data.
Once governance exists, we can build:
Now we can answer questions like:
- “Which components are likely to produce gaps next?”
- “What changes tend to precede ontology divergence?”
- “Which adapters are drifting over time?”
But more importantly:
> we can predict
where the system will fail to represent intent before it happens
We will build:
And eventually:
> proactive WorkRequest generation before divergence appears
If you want, next step I’d suggest we design:
> the
Divergence Memory Model (the dataset that makes prediction possible)
That’s the missing substrate between governance and true predictive capability.
